figures.label: Figure 6

figures.caption: Fluorescent microscopy of thermophilic bacteria G. kaustophilus HTA 426T cells. In (A) the control cells not treated with Geo6, while in (B) bacteria cells were treated with Geo6 for 30 min. The cells were stained using fluorescent dyes SYTO9 and PI. SYTO9 is capable of permeating the cell membranes and binding to the DNA of both live and dead cells. PI can only enter cells with damaged membranes and binds to the DNA. In (A) most of the cells exhibited green fluorescence, indicating that they were alive and healthy, with only a few cells showing red fluorescence due to membrane damage. In (B) all the cells exhibited red fluorescence, indicating that they were dead, as their membranes were no longer intact and the PI dye was able to bind to the DNA.

figures.caption: Three-dimensional structures of leaderless bacteriocins. The structure of Geo6 (A) was predicted using I-TASSER web tool. Experimentally determined 3D structures of AucA (B) and LnqQ (C) were derived from the RCSB PDB archive. The PDB numbers for AucA and LnqQ are 2N8O and 7P5R, respectively. In the visualizations, different colors are assigned to the different chains within the peptide structure. This color scheme distinguishes and visualizes the individual components of the peptide. The N-terminus is represented in blue, followed by green, yellow, orange, and finally red for the C-terminus.
